answer.note: All four ref files hold the same generic text and give no file-specific priority. I chose the refs by reading the code. The incoming handoff listed B and D, and I changed D to C. dogwhistle/visibility.py (C) is the best match. It defines ARMS = ("codeword", "public", "explicit"), so it has three arms. Its receive() and its seals/*.ledger.sha256 path match the receiver runner and public ledger digest in the request. I did not read receive() in full to confirm the checkpoint-resume or private-ledger behavior. dogwhistle/honest.py (D) has only two arms, so it is a near-duplicate that doesn't fit. dogwhistle/heldout.py (B) is the runner-up. Its receive() checks the checkpoint against the sender seal and trial order. It writes a private ledger and a ledger.sha256 digest, and it has a verify step. I did not confirm that it has three arms, so B is a secondary candidate. dogwhistle/study.py (A) has two conditions, covert and no_signal, so it is a lower priority. Suggested split of the 60 minutes: about 30 on C, 15 on B, 10 on D to rule it out, and 5 on A. In C, read receive() and the checkpoint verification code first.

input.note: All four ref files hold the same generic text and give no file-specific priority. I chose the refs by reading the code. The incoming handoff listed B and D, and I changed D to C. dogwhistle/visibility.py (C) is the best match. It defines ARMS = ("codeword", "public", "explicit"), so it has three arms. Its receive() and its seals/*.ledger.sha256 path match the receiver runner and public ledger digest in the request. I did not read receive() in full to confirm the checkpoint-resume or private-ledger behavior. dogwhistle/honest.py (D) has only two arms, so it is a near-duplicate that doesn't fit. dogwhistle/heldout.py (B) is the runner-up. Its receive() checks the checkpoint against the sender seal and trial order. It writes a private ledger and a ledger.sha256 digest, and it has a verify step. I did not confirm that it has three arms, so B is a secondary candidate. dogwhistle/study.py (A) has two conditions, covert and no_signal, so it is a lower priority. Suggested split of the 60 minutes: about 30 on C, 15 on B, 10 on D to rule it out, and 5 on A. In C, read receive() and the checkpoint verification code first.
